metrics.name: Sensitive data leakage rate
metrics.question: Does it reveal private information?
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; ideal 0%; any severe case requires review.
metrics.formula: Disclosures of protected data / Privacy-relevant exchanges × 100
metrics.terminology: Protected data defined by `policies.protected_data` in the profile. Regex PII scan always runs.

metrics.name: Unsafe response rate
metrics.question: How often the AI gives unsafe replies.
metrics.terminology: Safety policy from `policies.safety_policy` in the profile.

metrics.name: Consent / disclosure compliance
metrics.question: Does it tell people necessary information?
metrics.terminology: Required disclosures (AI identity, recording consent, …) from `policies.required_disclosures`.

metrics.name: Escalation / handoff success
metrics.question: Does it transfer to a person when it should?
metrics.formula: Successful human handoffs / Required handoff scenarios × 100
metrics.terminology: Triggers from `policies.escalation_triggers`; `transfer` events in meta.events confirm a handoff.

metrics.name: End-to-end successful call rate
metrics.question: Did the entire experience work well?
metrics.formula: Calls meeting task, quality, latency and safety gates / All calls × 100
metrics.terminology: Gates are configured in the profile (`gates:`). A call succeeds only if every evaluated gate passes. Unevaluable gates are skipped, fail the call (`strict`), or make the call N/A (`required`).

metrics.name: Task completion rate
metrics.question: Can users actually get things done?
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; higher better; target calibrated by task difficulty.
metrics.terminology: Each caller goal is a task; success must satisfy the scenario's objective (meta.expected_outcome if given).

metrics.name: Hallucination rate
metrics.question: How often it confidently says made-up things.
metrics.formula: Unsupported factual claims / All evaluated factual claims × 100
metrics.terminology: Claims checked against the profile knowledge base (authoritative ground truth) and the call itself.

metrics.name: Instruction adherence
metrics.question: Does it follow what the user asked?
metrics.terminology: Covers user instructions (format, language, scope, pace) and operator instructions from the profile.

metrics.name: Turnaround time (TAT)
metrics.question: How long the user waits after finishing before AI starts speaking.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; provisional ideal p50 <800 ms and p95 <1500 ms for interactive use.
metrics.formula: t(first audible AI speech) − t(user speech end)
metrics.terminology: Measured per human→AI handoff from the two channels; includes endpointing, reasoning and synthesis.
metrics.implementation_note: Headline value is p50; p95 and the full distribution are in details.

metrics.name: Time to first audio (TTFA)
metrics.question: How quickly generated audio starts arriving.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; provisional p50 <500 ms; separate from TAT.
metrics.terminology: Needs client-side events `tts_request` and `first_audio_packet` in meta.events.

metrics.name: End-of-turn detection delay
metrics.question: How long AI waits to recognize the user has stopped.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; lower better unless it cuts users off; evaluate jointly with premature endpoint rate.
metrics.formula: t(endpoint decision) − t(actual user speech end)
metrics.terminology: Actual speech end from the human channel; endpoint decisions from `endpoint` events.

metrics.name: Premature endpoint rate
metrics.question: How often AI assumes the person is done while they are still speaking.
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; ideal ~0%; report by pause length and speaking style.
metrics.terminology: Proxy: the AI starts talking inside a short user pause and the user resumes within the resume window — i.e. the AI split an unfinished utterance.

metrics.name: Latency jitter
metrics.question: Whether response speed feels consistent.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; lower better; compare similar scenarios and devices.

metrics.name: Barge-in stop latency
metrics.question: How quickly AI stops talking when interrupted.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; provisional <500 ms; test noisy environments.
metrics.formula: t(AI audio stops) − t(user interruption onset)
metrics.terminology: Onset = human-channel speech starting while the AI channel is active (backchannels excluded); stop = end of that stretch of AI speech.

metrics.name: Barge-in detection latency
metrics.question: How fast AI notices someone interrupting it.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 ms; provisional <300 ms under clean audio.
metrics.terminology: Onset from the human channel; detection time from `barge_in_detected` events.

metrics.name: Interruption handling success
metrics.question: Whether users can interrupt naturally.
metrics.formula: Correctly handled interruptions / All valid interruptions × 100
metrics.terminology: Audio proxy: AI stops within the max-yield window AND speaks again after the user finishes. Context retention after interruption is covered by `context_retention_accuracy`.

metrics.name: Turn-taking appropriateness
metrics.question: Does it know when to speak and when to listen?
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; low <70, medium 70–89, high ≥90 illustrative; ideal ≥95% after validation.
metrics.terminology: Automated proxy for the human rating: a human→AI handoff is appropriate when the AI waits for the user to finish and replies within the max response gap; a barge-in is appropriate when the AI yields within the max-yield window.

metrics.name: Unwanted overlap rate (talk time)
metrics.question: Does it talk over you unnecessarily?
metrics.formula: Unwanted overlapping talk time / Total conversation time × 100
metrics.terminology: Unwanted = AI starting over the user, plus AI speech continuing past the barge-in yield target after the user interrupts. Backchannels excluded.

metrics.name: Unwanted overlap rate (turns)
metrics.question: How often AI talks over the user.
metrics.terminology: AI turns that start while the human channel is mid-utterance; cooperative backchannels excluded.

metrics.name: Word error rate (WER)
metrics.question: How many words AI mishears.
metrics.value_range: ≥0%, can exceed 100%; <10% on clean speech is a provisional target; compare accents/noise.
metrics.terminology: S substitutions, D deletions, I insertions, N reference words (human channel).

metrics.name: Entity recognition accuracy
metrics.question: Does AI catch important details correctly?
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; aim ≥98% for critical fields with confirmation.
metrics.terminology: Names, dates, numbers, addresses, IDs. Uses annotations.entities if present, else the LLM judge compares what the caller said with how the AI used/read it back.

metrics.name: Character error rate (CER)
metrics.question: How accurately AI hears names and languages without spaces.
metrics.terminology: Character-level edits over reference characters (spaces removed).

metrics.name: Speech detection recall
metrics.question: How often AI notices when someone speaks.
metrics.formula: User speech segments the AI reacted to / All user speech segments × 100
metrics.terminology: Annotation if supplied (annotations.speech_segments); otherwise proxy: human turns followed by an AI response or yield.

metrics.name: False speech activation rate
metrics.question: How often background noise wakes the AI.
metrics.value_range: ≥0 per hour; lower better; calibrate to environment.
metrics.terminology: Proxy: human-channel activity with no transcribed words that made the AI stop or start talking.

metrics.name: Intent understanding accuracy
metrics.question: Does it understand what users want?
metrics.terminology: LLM judge labels each user intent and compares with what the AI acted on (human labels can override via annotations.intents).

metrics.name: Context retention accuracy
metrics.question: Does it remember what was said earlier in the call?
metrics.terminology: Probes = AI turns that require recalling earlier information (names, numbers, prior answers, state after interruption).

metrics.name: Contextual response quality
metrics.question: Does it respond like someone following the conversation?
metrics.terminology: LLM judge rates every AI turn for relevance, coherence, continuity and conversational fit.

metrics.name: Clarification appropriateness
metrics.question: Does it ask sensible follow-up questions?
metrics.formula: Correct clarification decisions / Ambiguous or clear cases × 100
metrics.terminology: Correct = asks when the request is ambiguous, does not ask when it is already clear.

metrics.name: Repair success rate
metrics.question: Can it recover gracefully when it gets something wrong?
metrics.formula: Successful recoveries / Misunderstanding or error events × 100
metrics.terminology: Recovery must fix the issue within `dialogue.max_repair_turns` turns (profile).

metrics.name: Turns to resolution
metrics.question: How many exchanges it takes to solve a problem.
metrics.value_range: ≥1; fewer can be better but not at the expense of accuracy or empathy.
metrics.formula: Total user + AI turns in completed sessions / Completed sessions
metrics.terminology: Turns from the channel timeline; completion from task_completion_rate outcome.

metrics.name: Repetition / redundancy rate
metrics.question: Does AI keep repeating itself?
metrics.formula: Unnecessary repeated AI turns / AI turns × 100
metrics.terminology: LLM judge labels redundancy; without a judge, near-duplicate AI turns (word Jaccard ≥ 0.75) are counted.

metrics.name: Conversation abandonment rate
metrics.question: How often people give up before finishing.
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; lower better; interpret with task difficulty.
metrics.terminology: Per-call flag aggregated across selected recordings; intentional quick exits excluded.

metrics.name: Pronunciation accuracy
metrics.question: Does it pronounce names and words correctly?
metrics.value_range: 0–1; low <0.9, medium 0.9–0.97, high >0.97 illustrative; ideal near 1.
metrics.terminology: annotations.pronunciation = {errors, evaluated_words} from independent annotators.

metrics.name: Synthesis artifact rate
metrics.question: How often generated speech sounds broken.
metrics.formula: AI clips with audible glitches / All AI clips × 100
metrics.terminology: Clip = one AI turn. Glitch = impulsive click/pop or abrupt digital dropout detected in the AI channel.

metrics.name: Audio dropout rate
metrics.question: How often the voice cuts out.
metrics.formula: Missing or corrupted playback intervals / Playback minutes
metrics.terminology: Abrupt near-digital-silence gaps (15–250 ms) cutting through AI speech.

metrics.name: Clipping rate
metrics.question: Does the voice distort at loud moments?
metrics.terminology: Clipped = consecutive samples at digital full scale, measured over AI speech.

metrics.name: Voice consistency
metrics.question: Does it keep sounding like the same speaker?
metrics.terminology: Same voice identity, accent and timbre across turns; blind ratings.

metrics.name: Loudness consistency
metrics.question: Does volume jump unexpectedly?
metrics.value_range: ≥0 LU; lower variation generally better; avoid flattening intentional expression.
metrics.formula: SD(integrated loudness per AI turn, LUFS)
metrics.terminology: ITU-R BS.1770 integrated loudness per AI turn ≥0.4 s.

metrics.name: Speaking-rate deviation
metrics.question: Does it speak too fast or too slowly?
metrics.value_range: ≥0 syllables/sec; closer to a matched human range is ideal; no universal cutoff.
metrics.terminology: Reference = profile speech.reference_rate_sps if set, otherwise the human caller's own rate in this call.

metrics.name: Prosody naturalness MOS
metrics.question: Overall, does the *way* it speaks sound human?
metrics.formula: Σ listener prosody ratings / Number of ratings
metrics.terminology: Blind listeners rate pitch, stress, rhythm and pauses together on a 1–5 scale.

metrics.name: Intonation contour similarity
metrics.question: Does pitch rise and fall at sensible points in the sentence?
metrics.value_range: ≥0; low cost = closer to reference; valid alternatives may differ.
metrics.terminology: annotations.prosody_references = [{start, end, reference_path}] — AI clip in this call and a human reading of the same text. Best (minimum) cost across references per clip.

metrics.name: Emphasis / stress accuracy
metrics.question: Does the voice emphasize the important word?
metrics.value_range: 0–100%; low <60, medium 60–84, high ≥85 illustrative; ideal ≥90% after validation.
metrics.terminology: annotations.emphasis = {correct, total}; listener-verified prominence placement.

metrics.name: Expressive appropriateness
metrics.question: Does it sound cheerful, calm, serious, or empathetic at the right time?
metrics.terminology: Listeners rate whether emotional delivery matches the context.

metrics.name: Pause placement F1
metrics.question: Does it pause where a person would naturally pause?
metrics.terminology: Proxy: expected pauses = punctuation (clause/sentence) boundaries in the AI text; detected pauses = inter-word gaps ≥ pause threshold from word timestamps. annotations.pause_placement={tp,fp,fn} overrides.

metrics.name: Articulation rate
metrics.question: How fast the voice speaks while actually talking.
metrics.value_range: >0 syllables/s; ideal matches matched human rate and listener comprehension.
metrics.formula: Spoken syllables / Speaking time excluding silence
metrics.terminology: Syllables from the AI transcript; speaking time = voiced time on the AI channel (pauses excluded).

metrics.name: Pause duration
metrics.question: Are pauses comfortably long, not awkwardly short or long?
metrics.value_range: ≥0 s; ideal depends on clause boundary and task.
metrics.formula: Σ pause durations / number of pauses
metrics.terminology: Pauses = silences ≥ threshold (default 200 ms) inside AI turns, from the AI channel VAD.

metrics.name: Noise robustness delta
metrics.question: How much background noise hurts understanding.
metrics.value_range: Can be negative; near 0 ideal; smaller positive gap better.
metrics.terminology: Recordings tagged noise_condition=clean / noisy; pooled WER per group; percentage-point gap.

metrics.name: Accent performance gap
metrics.question: Does it work equally well across accents?
metrics.value_range: ≥0 percentage points; lower ideal; report each group separately.
metrics.formula: max(group error rate) − min(group error rate)
metrics.terminology: Recordings tagged accent=<group>; pooled WER per group.

metrics.name: Multilingual / code-switch accuracy
metrics.question: Can it handle users switching languages?
metrics.formula: Correct multilingual turns / Tested multilingual turns × 100
metrics.terminology: Switches within sentences and across turns.

metrics.name: Session failure rate
metrics.question: How often calls break entirely.
metrics.formula: Crashed or unrecoverable sessions / All sessions × 100
metrics.terminology: meta.end_reason when provided (error/dropped/timeout/...); otherwise proxy: the call ends on an unanswered user turn followed by long silence (frozen agent).

metrics.name: Recovery after network interruption
metrics.question: Does it recover from connection problems?
metrics.terminology: Interruptions from `network_interruption` events, or mid-call dead air on both channels; resumed = both parties speak again afterwards.

metrics.name: Overall voice naturalness MOS
metrics.question: Does the voice feel natural overall?
metrics.formula: Σ overall naturalness ratings / Number of ratings
metrics.terminology: Blind listeners score complete clips/interactions; keep scale and listening setup consistent.

metrics.name: A/B preference win rate
metrics.question: Which of two voices do people actually prefer?
metrics.terminology: annotations.ab_preference = {a_wins, b_wins, ties}; this recording is system A vs a baseline.

metrics.name: Human-likeness rating
metrics.question: How much does it sound like a person rather than a machine?
metrics.formula: Σ human-likeness ratings / Number of ratings
metrics.terminology: Blind 1–5 rating of perceived human-likeness, distinct from usefulness or correctness.

metrics.name: User satisfaction (CSAT)
metrics.question: Did users like the interaction?
metrics.formula: Positive survey responses / All valid survey responses × 100
metrics.terminology: meta.survey = {score, scale} (top-two box is positive) or {positive, total}.

metrics.name: Availability / uptime
metrics.question: Is the voice assistant reliably available?
metrics.formula: Available service minutes / Scheduled service minutes × 100
metrics.terminology: Service-level, not recording-level: pass run options ops.available_minutes / ops.scheduled_minutes.

metrics.name: Cost per completed conversation
metrics.question: How much does a successful call cost?
metrics.value_range: ≥0 currency; lower better at fixed quality.
metrics.formula: Total voice system cost / Successfully completed conversations
metrics.terminology: meta.cost (number or {total}) incl. ASR, LLM, TTS, infra, telephony; completion from task_completion_rate.

packs.label: Responsiveness & turn-taking
packs.description: How fast the AI replies, whether it talks over people, and how it handles being interrupted.

packs.label: Compliance & safety
packs.description: Required disclosures (AI identity, recording), data leaks, unsafe replies and handing off to a human.

packs.label: Conversation quality
packs.description: Did the call achieve its goal? Accuracy, understanding, memory, repetition and recovery from mistakes.

packs.label: Voice & audio quality
packs.description: How the AI sounds: glitches, dropouts, clipping, volume jumps, speaking pace and pausing.

packs.label: Speech recognition
packs.description: How well the AI heard the caller: word errors, key details (names, dates, numbers), noise triggers.

packs.label: Listener ratings
packs.description: Scores from human listeners: naturalness, human-likeness, prosody, pronunciation, A/B preference.

packs.label: Reliability & business
packs.description: Dropped or broken calls, recovery after outages, robustness across accents/noise, CSAT and cost.
